{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts lag behind price turning points, especially at market bottoms where they undershoot the true bottom by 0.3-0.7 on average",
    "When sentiment turns positive, model forecasts are too slow to respond, creating persistent underperformance vs true prices",
    "Mean reversion bias in forecasts causes overshooting when prices deviate far from historical averages",
    "Sentiment indicators have highest predictive value at price extremes (bottoms (0.00-0.33) and tops (0.67-1.00)), with weak signal at mid-range sentiment",
    "Model forecast level bias varies with price regime - undershoots bottoms more than tops by ~0.3-0.5 on average",
    "Sentiment alignment with forecast direction: positive sentiment requires higher forecast levels, negative sentiment requires lower levels to match true price drift",
    "Forecasts show excessive smoothness - true prices contain more volatility than model outputs, especially in the middle 50% of the forecast horizon"
] }
